extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and patent practitioners involved in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and binding procedural/substantive standards for conducting and responding to inter partes reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including what may be considered, how claims are examined, and form/content/timing requirements for Office actions and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner statement re submitted art and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner must provide an unequivocal statement as to why the art submitted makes at least one claim unpatentable, an amendment to such claim or claims, and an explanation as to how the amendment causes such claim or claims to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in addition to a factual accounting explaining why the information could not have been submitted earlier. Submission of patents and printed publications must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 (with fee) for withdrawal of the reexamination proceeding from the printing cycle for entry and consideration of the information submitted by the patent owner; a grantable petition must provide the requisite showing discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art per 37 CFR 1.98 and required forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of the patents and printed publications as provided for in 37 CFR 1.98; the examiner must list on form PTO-892 (or equivalent format) all prior art patents or printed publications cited in the decision on the request, applied in making rejections or cited as pertinent during the reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations listed on form PTO-892, and all citations not lined-through on any PTO/SB/08A/08B or PTO/SB/42 (or equivalent), will be printed on the reexamination certificate under 'References cited.' Prior art may have come to the examiner's attention because it was (A) of record from 37 CFR 1.501 submission prior to order date; (B) of record from earlier examination; (C) discovered by examiner during search; or (D) submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.948.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination in inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.906(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an inter partes reexamination proceeding will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes reexamination practice as to substance is the same as ex parte reexamination; however, procedure differs. Examiner must apply 35 U.S.C. 112 when subject matter is added or deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on enlargement of claim scope (37 CFR 1.906(b) and 35 U.S.C. 314)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an inter partes reexamination proceeding will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent; no proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope shall be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine presented claims under 35 U.S.C. 314 to determine enlargement. A claim that is broader than each and every claim of the patent is considered broadening; a claim is broadened if it is broader in any one respect even if narrower in others. See MPEP §1412.03 for guidance on what constitutes broadening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible bases for reexamination rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections on art in reexamination proceedings may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications, or double patenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions used to determine substantial new question of patentability in ex parte reexamination apply equally to inter partes reexamination. Issues not based on patents/printed publications (e.g., conduct issues) are not to be resolved in reexamination (37 CFR 1.906(c)) and should be handled via reissue or other proceedings if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112 when claims/disclosure amended
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new or amended claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims of the reexamination proceeding are to be examined for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion of 112 examination in ex parte MPEP §2258 applies equally in inter partes reexamination. Ordinarily no 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection appears in the first Office action because patent owner amendments are prohibited prior to first action (37 CFR 1.939(b)); exceptions exist when merged with an existing reexamination containing an amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for determining enlargement of scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim presented in a reexamination enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent being reexamined where the claim is broader than each and every claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §1412.03 for guidance on what is broadening. If a claim is considered broadening for reissue purposes, it is likewise broadening in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendments must not enlarge claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification is amended in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner should ensure that the amendment to the specification does not enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment to the specification can enlarge claim scope by redefining the scope of terms in a claim even where the claims themselves are not amended; examiner should review for such redefinitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection procedure for claims that enlarge scope (35 U.S.C. 314(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim which enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.03.01 is employed when making the rejection. Examiner must identify and explain the claim limitations considered to broaden the scope (see bracket 2 in form paragraph and MPEP §2658).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims subject to prior Office or court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some patent claims being reexamined have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, those claims should be identified and handled as described in MPEP §2642; claims finally held invalid by a Federal Court after all appeals will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grounds set forth in a prior decision are not based on patents/printed publications, examiner's Office action should state the claims have not been examined as to those grounds and applicable portions of 35 U.S.C. 112. See In re Knight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination limited to 'live' claims requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office’s determination will generally be limited solely to a review of the 'live' claims (existing claims not held invalid by a final decision) for which reexamination has been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester had the opportunity to include all claims in its request. 35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2) requires the requester to set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested; failure to do so generally precludes reexamination of that claim. The Office may in its discretion reexamine non-requested claims or initiate reexamination on its own (35 U.S.C. 303(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirements not proper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding since no statutory basis exists for restriction in such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of claims to a separate and distinct invention would be considered enlargement of claim scope. See Ex parte Wikdahl and MPEP §1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary amendments necessary to patentability may be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters ancillary to reexamination which are necessary and incident to patentability will be considered; amendments may be made to the specification to correct, for example, an inadvertent failure to claim foreign priority or continuing status if necessary to overcome a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments should be limited to those necessary to address patentability issues raised by prior art or other reexamination matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign and domestic priority in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may obtain foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) by submitting the certified copy; may perfect earlier priority or submit both claim and certified copy for the first time in reexamination, subject to petition requirements for certain patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent matured from an application filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, and first-time submission of both claim for priority and certified copy is necessary, patent owner must file a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed priority claim under 37 CFR 1.55(c). Correcting benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 for applications on/after Nov 29, 2000 requires petition under 37 CFR 1.78(a)(3). Reexamination cannot be employed to add or correct certain benefit claims (e.g., 119(e)) for patents matured from applications filed on/after Nov 29, 2000. No renewal of previously made priority/benefit claims is necessary during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination (37 CFR 1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination via petition under 37 CFR 1.324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a petition is granted, a Certificate of Correction indicating the change of inventorship will not be separately issued because the reexamination certificate will contain the appropriate change-of-inventorship information (merged with the reexamination certificate). See MPEP §1481.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of affidavits in reexamination (37 CFR 1.131/1.132/1.130)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132 may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding, but an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131 may not be used to 'swear back' of a reference patent if the reference patent claims the same invention as the patent undergoing reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, patent owner may, if appropriate, seek to raise the issue via an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.130 (see MPEP §718) or in an interference proceeding via an appropriate reissue application if permissible (see MPEP §1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not within scope of reexamination (37 CFR 1.906(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions other than those indicated (e.g., patentability based on patents/printed publications and 35 U.S.C. 112) — such as public use, on sale, conduct issues, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), etc. — if raised by the patent owner or third party requester will be noted by the examiner but not resolved in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may consider filing a reissue application to have such issues considered and resolved. If such issues are independently discovered by the examiner but not raised by the parties, they will not be noted in an Office action under 37 CFR 1.906(c). Use form paragraph 26.03 to indicate an issue is not within the scope of reexamination and advise about possible reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for reexamination on patents after reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reexamination filed on a patent after it has been reissued will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reexamine a reissued patent, a new request based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent must be filed. Any amendment made by the patent owner during reexamination should treat changes made by the granted reissue patent as the text of the patent, including bracketing/underlining with respect to reissue changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty in taking up a reexamination (37 CFR 1.104(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up a patent in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention; examination shall be complete with respect to applicable statutes and rules, patentability, and matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant/patent owner and requester will be notified of the examiner's action; reasons for adverse action/objections will be stated and references given as may be useful in judging propriety of continuing prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (misjoinder, fundamental defects, etc.) action may be limited to such matters before further action is made; matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rejection is based on facts within personal knowledge of an Office employee, data shall be as specific as possible and may require supporting affidavit subject to contradiction/explanation by applicant affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards when rejecting claims (37 CFR 1.104(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, the claims considered unpatentable will be rejected. In rejecting claims for novelty or obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his/her command and, when a reference is complex, designate the particular part relied upon 'as nearly as practicable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pertinency of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified. Examiner may rely on admissions by applicant/patent owner and on facts within his/her knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of subject matter developed by another person (35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f),(g) and 103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e),(f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned or subject to obligation of assignment at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents/applications on/after Dec 10, 2004, a claimed invention and subject matter are deemed commonly owned for purposes of this exception if (A) made by parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the claimed invention date, (B) made as a result of activities within the agreement's scope, and (C) the patent application discloses or is amended to disclose the parties' names. To overcome a 103 rejection based on 102(e)/(f)/(g) subject matter, applicant must provide a statement to that effect as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of references details (37 CFR 1.104(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When domestic patents are cited, their numbers, dates, and patentees' names will be stated; published applications' publication number, date, and applicants' names must be stated; foreign publications/patents must have nationality, numbers, dates, and patentee names stated; printed publications must include author, title, date, pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only part of a foreign document is involved, identify particular pages/sheets containing the parts relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance must be set forth when unclear (37 CFR 1.104(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record does not make clear his/her reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning; the applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of a separate communication. Failure by the examiner to respond to any commenting statement does not give rise to any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and preparation of the first Office action (ten-week rule and form paragraph 26.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first Office action on the merits will ordinarily be mailed together with the order granting reexamination; if impractical it may be mailed later, but the order must be mailed within ten weeks of the filing date of the request; when first action is not mailed with the order, the order must indicate an Office action will issue in due course and form paragraph 26.04 should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where not mailed with the order, the Office action should be issued within two months from mailing of the order (or within one month from the merger decision if awaiting merger).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of first action on the merits (ACP vs rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where all patent claims are found patentable in the first action, the examiner will issue an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP). Where one or more claims are rejected, the first Office action will be similar to a first action in an application but inter partes practice, forms and time periods apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes reexamination forms and special time periods must be used; both patent owner and third party requester must be sent a copy of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for the first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s first Office action should be comprehensive and address all issues as to the prior art patents and/or printed publications, clearly setting forth each ground of rejection/objection and the reasons supporting them, and each determination favorable to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The action should respond to the substance of each argument raised by the third party requester pursuant to 37 CFR 1.915 and address any other issues proper for reexamination. If request includes a claim chart, examiner may incorporate it but must carefully review to ensure incorporated items clearly and completely address patentability. The first action should caution the patent owner that a complete response is required because the next action is expected to be an ACP and that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after an ACP; include form paragraph 26.05 and 26.73 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on patent owner amendment prior to first Office action (37 CFR 1.939(b)) and effect on 112 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily there will be no patent owner amendment to address in the first Office action because 37 CFR 1.939(b) prohibits a patent owner amendment prior to first Office action; thus the first Office action will ordinarily contain no rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only exception is when the reexamination is merged with an existing proceeding that already contains an amendment; in that case, 112 issues raised by the amendment and any improper broadening under 35 U.S.C. 314 will be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to adopt requester-proposed rejections when not merely cumulative
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner is not to refuse to adopt a rejection properly proposed by the requester as being cumulative to other rejections applied; any such proposed rejection must be adopted to preserve parties’ appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each rejection proposed by the third party requester that the examiner refuses to adopt, reasons why the rejection is not appropriate must be clearly stated. Comprehensive reasons for patentability must be given for determinations favorable to patentability. See MPEP §1302.14 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for responsive submissions to first Office action (form paragraph 26.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers including amendments, affidavits/declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability must be submitted in response to the first Office action to ensure full consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions after the next Office action (intended to be an ACP) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (d), which will be strictly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and administrative requirements for first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the first Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office action cover sheet is PTOL-2064; where first Office action is a first action, the space for the date of the communication to which the Office action is responsive should not be filled in (the order, not the first action, responds to the request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence routing and contact information (form paragraph 26.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence relating to the inter partes reexamination proceeding should be directed to the Central Reexamination Unit at the specified mailing address, fax number, or hand delivery location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Central Reexamination Unit contact details (mail, fax, hand delivery) and telephone number for inquiries; use PTOL-2064 as Office action cover sheet.
